items.title: Indoor air pollution and health outcomes in women in developing Asian countries: a systematic review.
items.key: All selection and data extraction processes were carried out independently by two reviewers. Strong and consistent evidence was found across the 28 included studies. IAP exposure was significantly associated with multi-systemic health damage, including increased respiratory symptoms (aOR=3.0), decreased lung function, and adverse reproductive outcomes such as a higher risk of birth defects (aOR up to 7.09) and stillbirth (aOR=1.34). Furthermore, exposure was linked to increased cardio-metabolic disease risk, genotoxicity, and significant cognitive decline. Thus, future policies and interventions are urgently needed to mitigate this preventable burden of disease.

items.key: CONCLUSION: Perioperative analgesic strategies may reduce early postoperative pain after hysterectomy, although consistent benefits were not demonstrated at 24 hours. High-quality studies are warranted to establish standardized multimodal protocols and assess longer-term pain outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Women with PCOS face a substantial risk of preterm birth, driven by a dual pathway of intrinsic metabolic/androgenic dysfunction and extrinsic factors like assisted reproductive technology. items.title: Effectiveness of Prenatal Screening for Gestational Diabetes: A Narrative Review.
items.key: Particular attention was given to the clinical implications of identifying milder degrees of dysglycemia and to the economic and practical consequences of different screening approaches. This review concluded that prenatal GDM screening should aim to achieve clinically meaningful detection while minimizing unnecessary intervention and patient burden. Future research should focus on standardized outcomes, simplified and accessible screening approaches, and context-specific strategies that integrate clinical effectiveness, economic considerations, and healthcare resources.

items.title: Surveillance strategies for the early detection of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors in neurofibromatosis type 1: a systematic review.
items.key: One retrospective imaging study traced 91% of MPNSTs to a pre-existing distinct nodular lesion. Diffusion-weighted MRI and FDG-PET discriminated benign from malignant tumors with high sensitivity in symptomatic referral cohorts, with threshold-dependent specificity. Harms were inconsistently reported. Certainty was very low for surveillance impact and harms and low for diagnostic accuracy. Current evidence is insufficient to establish whether surveillance improves outcomes; this review informs the design of prospective trials and the next revision of international surveillance guidelines.

items.title: The Role of the cGAS-STING Pathway in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
items.key: Additional upstream mechanisms included gut microbiota-associated metabolic disruption and lead-induced SOD2 dysfunction. STING inhibition or knockout and interventions targeting mitochondrial homeostasis, including ketogenic diet, β-hydroxybutyrate, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and SOD2 enhancement, attenuated inflammatory or PCOS-like phenotypes. Overall, STING may represent a molecular link between mitochondrial damage and inflammation in PCOS, although predominantly preclinical evidence warrants further clinical investigation.

items.title: Prenatal Genetics and Investigational in Utero Gene Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease: Clinical, Ethical, and Justice Considerations.
items.key: There is currently no evidence that prenatal somatic gene therapy is cost-effective or would overcome access barriers. Its reliance on fetal medicine, molecular, and manufacturing infrastructure could initially widen disparities. Clinical translation would be ethically defensible only after disease-specific comparative evidence, independent oversight, non-directive consent, lifelong follow-up and a credible equitable-access plan. Strengthening newborn screening and proven care remains the immediate justice priority.

items.title: A Narrative Review of Intravesical OnabotulinumtoxinA for the Treatment of Overactive Bladder and Practical Implications for UK-Based Practice: Do Injection Distribution and Site Matter?
items.key: This narrative review considers what the current literature on injection number, distribution and depth means for UK outpatient practice, and whether the conventional technique remains the best-supported approach or whether alternative, simpler techniques could make the procedure quicker and more tolerable without loss of effectiveness. We conclude that total dose, rather than how it is distributed, appears to be the main determinant of clinical response, and we consider the practical implications of this for UK services, along with the gaps in the evidence that UK-generated research could address.

items.title: Building Demand for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination in India: A Review of the Behavioural and Social Drivers of Parental and Community Acceptance.

items.title: Immune cell mediated fibrosis after kidney transplantation: mechanisms and emerging immunomodulatory therapies.
items.key: Established immunosuppression remains essential for preventing immune mediated graft injury, whereas regulatory T cell therapies, macrophage state modulation, cytokine blockade, and CD38 directed therapy remain investigational. None has been proven to reverse established allograft fibrosis. Future diagnosis and treatment should integrate Banff histology, donor specific antibodies, donor derived cell free DNA, urinary chemokines, and biopsy-based transcriptomics. Clinical trials should determine whether targeted immunomodulation can slow the progression of allograft fibrosis and preserve long-term graft function and survival.

items.title: Modernizing reporting and communication of isolated echogenic intracardiac foci and choroid plexus cysts in the cell-free DNA era.
items.key: In pregnancies with low-risk cfDNA results and a normal detailed fetal anatomic survey, isolated EIF and CPCs should be regarded as benign findings without clinical significance. Contemporary evidence no longer supports the routine reporting and communication of these findings in the context of aneuploidy risk. When disclosure occurs, communication should be non-alarmist, emphasize that these are normal variants, and avoid terminology suggesting increased risk for chromosomal abnormalities. Aligning reporting and communication with current evidence has the potential to reduce patient harm while promoting patient-centered prenatal care.

items.title: Laparoscopic versus robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: trifecta outcomes in prostate cancer surgery.
items.key: Within the two approaches, oncological outcomes such as positive surgical margin and biochemical recurrence were comparable. There was reduced postoperative pain, faster recovery, and higher satisfaction scores associated with RARP. The choice between RARP and LRP should be individualized. Further research should focus on integrating AI, AR and ePROMSs to improve surgical care. RARP offers advantages in early functional recovery, while long-term oncological outcomes remain comparable between techniques.

items.title: DDX3X and DDX3Y in human reproduction and development: from molecular mechanisms to clinical implications.

The narrow, near-categorical male phenotype and the graded, multisystem female one may reflect this shared activity acting at different developmental moments. What the two phenotypes share is that activity, not a common causal lesion.

items.title: Pathophysiological mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic opportunities in endometriosis.
items.key: We further examine the roles of aberrant steroid hormone signaling, angiogenesis, and lymphangiogenesis in lesion maintenance and progression, as well as how these interconnected processes contribute to lesion heterogeneity and treatment resistance. Finally, we highlight how emerging multi-omics approaches and patient-derived organoid and assembloid models may facilitate mechanistic validation, biomarker discovery, and therapeutic development. By connecting the mechanisms of lesion initiation and progression with current therapeutic limitations, this review provides a framework for developing more precise, mechanism-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

Patient-derived organoids, CRISPR/Cas9 screening, and circulating tumor DNA monitoring enable clinical translation, supporting rationally designed combinations over sequential monotherapy and reframing AKT from a poor-prognosis marker to a therapeutic target in recurrent, chemoresistant ovarian cancer.

items.title: Endometriosis, a high-risk obstetric condition: pathophysiology of the maternal-placenta axis.

Reframing endometriosis as a potential vascular risk equivalent opens perspectives for prospective trials on immune-modulatory therapies and personalized biomarkers, potentially improving maternal-fetal outcomes in this high-burden population.

items.title: Motile ciliopathies: a focus on primary ciliary dyskinesia.
items.key: Currently, treatment options for PCD are limited, with prevalent therapies mainly aimed at limiting lung damage. In this review, we will introduce motile cilia disorders under the umbrella of PCD and discuss key genetic factors involved in their aetiology, also highlighting what we currently know about PCD in the context of the Indian population. We will also explore how motile cilia have been linked to other diseases, such as COVID-19. Lastly, we will discuss how PCD is being researched and how these investigations could provide better treatment options, and possibly, a cure for the disease in the years ahead.

items.title: Current perspective in the pharmacological management of platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
items.key:
rgeted narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted, including literature available up to 27 July 2026.
EXPERT OPINION: Treatment should move beyond a fixed platinum-free interval toward an individualized assessment of platinum appropriateness. The new regimens are not interchangeable and should not be ranked by indirect comparisons. Biomarker availability, previous therapy, residual toxicity, disease kinetics, and patient priorities should guide selection. Over the next five years, the main challenge will be treatment sequencing and the development of dynamic models that estimate the probability of benefit from platinum and non-platinum options at each recurrence.

items.title: Antimuscarinic medication use and risk of glaucoma in patients with overactive bladder: a literature review and disproportionality analysis using individual case safety reports from FAERS.

These findings suggest that certain antimuscarinics, particularly tolterodine, darifenacin, and fesoterodine, may be associated with an increased risk of glaucoma and warrant further pharmacoepidemiologic investigation to confirm safety and inform prescribing decisions.

items.title: Underrecognised legacies of preeclampsia: a biosocial DOHaD perspective for research in sub-Saharan Africa.
items.key: We review evidence and identify four priority domains for investigation: understanding context-specific causes and mechanisms; improving detection, care-seeking, and health system pathways; examining long-term maternal and offspring outcomes; and strengthening research infrastructures. We argue that advancing research on preeclampsia in SSA requires interdisciplinary approaches that integrate biological, clinical, epidemiological, and qualitative research. Such a research agenda has the potential to improve understanding of preeclampsia beyond its acute manifestations and to inform more equitable strategies for maternal and child health across the life course.

items.title: Sexual Violence/Abuse and Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review of the Relationship.
items.key: Findings point to a need for prevention strategies that consider how gender intersects with exposure to sexual violence/abuse. The review also suggests elevated co-occurrence between cervical cancer and sexual violence/abuse relative to global population estimates (~10% intimate-partner violence and ~6% non-partner violence). Limitations include small samples and measurement heterogeneity. Findings support co-produced, survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches to cervical cancer prevention and oncology care that address barriers to healthcare engagement. Larger studies using validated measures and confounder-aware designs are needed.

items.title: Ferric derisomaltose for the treatment of iron deficiency with or without anemia in women's health: an expert review.
items.key: Although efficacy is largely comparable among IV iron formulations when equivalent doses are used, there are factors that distinguish certain IV iron formulations from others. This review aims to discuss available evidence for the treatment of ID/IDA in women with ferric derisomaltose (FDI; a high-dose IV iron formulation), focusing on AUB, pregnancy, and PPH. Based on existing data, FDI represents a clinically-effective option for iron repletion in these contexts, and a low risk of hypersensitivity reactions and hypophosphatemia. There is scope for further research within the field of ID/IDA in women's health to address unmet needs and evidence gaps across the patient care pathway.

items.title: Aging-related immune remodeling in ovarian cancer: endocrine cues, cellular senescence, and tumor-immune crosstalk.

This review highlights an evidence framework based on histotype, tissue compartment, treatment exposure, functional age, and longitudinal sampling. Progress requires prospective cohorts that include older and frail adults and jointly assess tumor biology, immune state, treatment toxicity, and clinical outcome.

items.title: Testosterone Therapy and Sexual Health in Men and Women: Is There a Role for Long-Acting Subcutaneous Pellets?
items.key: This narrative review describes the physiology of testosterone in both sexes, the diagnostic criteria and validated instruments used to assess sexual function, the trial evidence for testosterone therapy, and the pharmacology, effectiveness, and safety of pellets. Pellets are a reasonable option for selected hypogonadal men who do not seek fertility, accept a formulation that cannot be quickly reversed, and agree to hematocrit monitoring. In women, current guidance does not support their use, and any exception requires informed consent, close monitoring, and acknowledgment that it departs from that guidance.

items.title: Maternal-fetal considerations of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy.
items.key: Emerging evidence demonstrates that CFTRm cross the placenta and can be detected in cord blood, neonatal plasma, and infant tissues. However, the extent of fetal exposure, tissue accumulation and potential developmental implications remain incompletely understood. Herein, we emphasise the mechanistic and pharmacological evidence underlying fetal exposure to CFTRm . This review synthesises current evidence regarding the transplacental transfer, fetal exposure and developmental implications of CFTRm during pregnancy. We discuss emerging pharmacokinetic data, reported maternal and infant outcomes and key knowledge gaps that remain regarding the safety of in utero CFTRm exposure.

items.title: Popularity Without Proof: A Narrative Review of Peptide Adjuncts to Testosterone Therapy in Body Composition and Functional-Driven Use.
items.key: Evidence for restorative peptides, such as BPC-157 and TB-500, remains largely preclinical, with minimal to no data supporting their efficacy in humans. Variable product quality from unregulated sources is a cause for concern. Testosterone and peptide regimens are increasingly utilized despite significant gaps in the evidence. This necessitates distinguishing between established indications and experimental uses, and informed, nonjudgmental counseling as a harm-reduction strategy. The aim of this review is to examine the available human evidence regarding GH secretagogues and restorative peptides used as adjuncts to testosterone therapy, focusing on body composition, strength, and safety.

items.title: 3D and 4D Hysterosalpingo-Contrast Sonography: Advanced Tubal Patency Assessment.
items.key: This article is intended to serve as a practical guide to performing 3D-4D HyCoSy with microbubble contrast agents, including preparation, technical parameters, and findings interpretation. In addition, the authors compare HyCoSy with conventional techniques, review characteristic imaging patterns of tubal patency and occlusion, and discuss potential pitfalls and preventive strategies. As an advanced US technology combined with a dynamic functional perspective, 3D-4D HyCoSy represents a powerful, cost-effective, and patient-friendly tool for integrated fertility evaluation in modern radiology practices.

items.title: Maternal KIR-Fetal HLA-C Interactions in IVF and Pregnancy: Evidence, Clinical Implications, and Ethics; A Narrative Review.
items.key: Current guidelines do not recommend routine HLA-C matching or KIR-directed immune modulation for recurrent implantation failure (RIF). items.title: Prevalence and impact of urinary incontinence in Canada: a systematic review of the quantitative and qualitative literature and a meta-analysis of quantitative data.

items.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.

items.title: Prevalence and Predictors of Intrauterine Device Failure Among Women in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Scoping Review.

items.title: Mechanotransduction in the placental endothelium: molecular mechanisms and implications for pregnancy complications.
items.key: This review integrates current understanding of placental endothelial mechanotransduction, examines its dysregulation in pregnancy-related complications including PE, fetal growth restriction (FGR), and gestational hypertension (GH). While partial mechanistic overlap exists between these conditions, GH represents a distinct and generally milder clinical phenotype; fetoplacental endothelial-specific molecular features of GH remain largely uncharacterized and constitute an important knowledge gap. We further identify priorities for the development of mechanism-based precision interventions for PE, FGR and GH.

items.title: Ovarian rejuvenation: Ways to restart the ovaries: A narrative review.
items.key: Mounting evidence has suggested promising outcomes, such as restored hormone levels, increased follicle counts and maturation, and higher-quality oocytes. Besides, their working principles are based on countering fibrosis and inflammation, which often support the decline in ovarian function. While these methods aim to revive ovarian function under different circumstances, inconsistent findings are still being reported, emphasizing their uncertainty in practical terms. This review discusses novel therapies showing potential for ovarian rejuvenation and provides new insights into their specific roles in ameliorating ovarian conditions of various natures and at different stages.

items.title: Orchestrating implantation: endometrial receptivity as a convergence point of endocrine, metabolic, and immune signals.
items.key: tly, emerging evidence supports a conceptual shift from viewing impaired receptivity as the consequence of isolated molecular defects toward understanding it as a systems-level disruption of interconnected endocrine, metabolic, immune, and cellular networks, a common pathological feature across infertility-associated disorders such as endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome, chronic endometritis, and adenomyosis. Defining the temporal and spatial coordination of these networks may facilitate the development of more reliable biomarkers and mechanism-based, personalized strategies for assessing and restoring endometrial receptivity, ultimately improving implantation and reproductive outcomes.

items.title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
items.key: Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

CONCLUSIONS: In reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, GLP-1 receptor agonists may offer weight-loss benefits and improvements in central obesity compared with conventional regimens; however, these findings are derived from a small, clinically heterogeneous pool of trials with short follow-up and low-certainty evidence. The pooled estimates should therefore be interpreted with caution and considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

items.title: Is It Safe to Treat Patients with Botulinum Toxin A During the Peri-Conception Period of Pregnancy? A Systematic Review of the Literature.

One case of preterm labor with fetal renal anomaly and one case of fetal growth restriction were reported.
CONCLUSION: Peri-conception botulinum toxin exposure was not associated with increased adverse outcomes compared with population rates, though evidence is limited by small, heterogenous studies.

Text messaging, voice messaging, and video-based interventions demonstrated positive but nonsignificant effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Multicomponent technology-based educational interventions were more effective than single-modality approaches in improving cancer screening uptake among migrant women.

items.title: Uterine Sarcomas: Updates and Challenges.
items.key: They arise as mesenchymal tumors from muscle and connective tissues. The most common subtypes include uterine leiomyosarcoma at 63%, low-grade and high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma at 21%, and the remainder include the less common subtypes like undifferentiated uterine sarcoma, adenosarcoma, perivascular epithelioid cell tumor, SMARCA4-deficient uterine sarcoma, uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor, NTRK-rearranged sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor. Through a surgical lens, this review will explore the most current diagnostic criteria and management strategies available.

items.title: Systemic Lupus and Other Autoimmune Disorders During Pregnancy.
items.key: Patients require coordinated care with obstetrics, maternal fetal medicine, and rheumatology. Many drugs used for the care of rheumatologic conditions are safe in pregnancy, but detailed review should occur, ideally preconception, so the patient can be on the safest regimen while maintaining disease control. Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies particularly pose unique risks of neonatal lupus syndrome, including cardiac manifestations. Medical management is unique to each disease and includes ultrasounds and antenatal testing to optimize both maternal and fetal well-being and minimize perinatal risks.

items.title: Thrombocytopenia in Pregnancy: Diagnosis and Management.
items.key: In an uncomplicated pregnancy with platelet counts greater than 80 x 109/L, gestational thrombocytopenia is the most likely etiology. More severe thrombocytopenia, particularly those presenting in first or early second trimester, should prompt consideration of alternative causes including immune thrombocytopenia. When thrombocytopenia is accompanied by hemolytic anemia, patients should be evaluated for thrombotic microangiopathy. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, including pre-eclampsia and hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelet syndrome, are most common etiologies in late second and third trimesters.

items.title: Menopause and Sexual Health in Older Adults.
items.key: Menopause is a systemic endocrine transition characterized by estrogen deficiency, driving a cascade of vasomotor, musculoskeletal, and genitourinary sequelae in older women. Hormonal shifts, specifically declining estrogen and testosterone, contribute to vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and decreased libido. These physiologic changes are further complicated by comorbidities, polypharmacy, and functional limitations. Similarly, gradual testosterone decline in men may impair libido and erectile function. This review provides a clinically focused framework for the evaluation and management of sexual dysfunction in geriatric practice.

items.title: Hypogonadism in Older Men.
items.key: Hypogonadism in older men refers to the late-onset clinical syndrome of impaired androgen production and/or spermatogenesis. Aging in men is associated with a gradual decline in serum testosterone concentrations. Some older hypogonadal men may benefit from testosterone therapy while others may not. The decision of whether to prescribe testosterone for an older hypogonadal man should be based on the severity of hypogonadism, an assessment of the potential benefits and risks of treatment, and the patient's willingness to accept the risks of treatment and monitoring. The choice of testosterone formulation depends on the patient's preferences, pharmacokinetics, treatment burden, and cost.

items.title: Common Outpatient Procedures: Outpatient Gynecologic Procedures.
items.key: This review summarizes key outpatient gynecologic procedures, including cervical cancer screening, insertion and removal of intrauterine devices and contraceptive implants, and endometrial biopsies. Evidence-based approaches to pain management for intrauterine procedures are reviewed, including intracervical and paracervical blocks. Procedural pitfalls and strategies to reduce complications are discussed. Competence in these procedures enables timely, patient-centered preventative and reproductive care while minimizing need for specialist referral.

items.title: Polypharmacy and the ageing brain: Anticholinergic burden in the ageing population and the impact of gynaecological medications.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Although the evidence linking cumulative anticholinergic exposure with long-term cognitive decline and dementia remains inconsistent and predominantly observational, higher anticholinergic burden has been associated with adverse outcomes including delirium, drowsiness, and an increased risk of falls, particularly in older adults. Routine assessment, careful medication review, and appropriate deprescribing may reduce avoidable harm. Integrating burden assessment into prescribing systems and clinical decision-support tools may further promote safer pharmacotherapy in an ageing society.

Overall, current evidence supports a biologically plausible association between endometrial microbiome composition and reproductive outcomes following ART, but well-designed prospective studies using standardized methodologies are needed to determine whether endometrial microbial signatures can serve as clinically actionable biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

items.title: Neuroendocrine drivers of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and the modifying role of adiposity.
items.key: Given the high prevalence of obesity in PMOS, dampening of raised LH concentrations with obesity challenges its use as part of diagnostic criteria for PMOS in populations where obesity is prevalent. Obesity-induced metabolic dysfunction also leads to hyperinsulinaemia, which further exacerbates ovarian hyperandrogenism. The interplay between metabolic dysfunction and reproductive health is illustrated by weight-management interventions, which consistently improve ovulatory function in women with obesity and PMOS. Understanding the neuroendocrine impact of obesity on the pathophysiology of PMOS can inform both diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic targets.

items.title: Efficacy of dietary supplements in improving sperm parameters in men with infertility: a network meta-analysis.
items.key: For improving total sperm motility, the top five supplements were omega-3, curcumin nanomicelle, LAC, zinc, and ALA. For improving total sperm count, the top five supplements were ALA, curcumin nanomicelle, zinc, L-carnitine (LC), and LAC. Appropriate dietary supplements demonstrate significant efficacy in improving semen parameters in male patients with infertility. However, their efficacy varies across semen parameters. Zinc and omega-3 ranked relatively high across all six semen parameters. In clinical practice, the individual characteristics of different patients should be considered when selecting therapeutic agents and formulating personalized dietary supplement regimens.

items.title: Factors influencing parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination in Sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review.

Closing the region's HPV vaccination gap may require country and community-tailored, multicomponent strategies combining trusted-messenger communication, dedicated safety-concern counseling, and continued attention to cost and access barriers, particularly in under-studied countries and rural settings.

items.title: Genetic Counseling When One Partner Carries a CF-Causing Variant and the Other Has the Intronic IVS8-5T Variant.

Questions arise as to what information to provide about the likely outcome if the fetus or newborn has both variants in trans, as well as implications for future pregnancies and other family members. In this paper, we consider an approach to genetic counseling based on knowledge of CFTR biology and available clinical data.

items.title: GATA2: A Custodian of Endometrial Identity: Guarding the Uterine Lining in Health and Disease.
items.key: Acting in a cross-regulatory feedback loop with the progesterone receptor (PGR), GATA2 both maintains endometrial PGR expression and cooperates with PGR on chromatin to enable PGR signaling ensembles. Now, numerous studies are beginning to provide additional mechanistic insights into the critical roles of GATA2 in both normal reproductive biology and in the pathogenesis of multiple uterine disorders. Recently, GATA2 dysregulation has also been implicated in the progression of multiple uterine cancer subtypes. This review aims to organize the seminal findings on uterine GATA2 functions to date and plot a path forward toward resolving major unanswered questions in this rapidly evolving area.

We also analyze the chemico-biological interaction profiles of several small-molecule VEGFR2 inhibitors. This review article provides an overview of the latest advances in medicinal chemistry approaches to VEGFR2 inhibitors.

Emerging approaches, including PET/MRI, volumetric parameters, FAPI and other novel radiopharmaceuticals, and radiomics, are discussed as future directions in gynecologic oncology.

items.title: Ovarian function and fertility after childhood cancer: risk assessment in the era of novel treatments.
items.key: This review examines the effect of conventional cancer treatments on ovarian function and fertility, as well as the methods currently used to assess ovarian reserve in female childhood cancer survivors and preserve fertility. It also considers how evolving treatment strategies across major cancers affecting adolescents and young adults may influence reproductive outcomes. Particular attention is given to the limited evidence available on the reproductive effects of targeted treatments and immunotherapies. Further prospective studies integrating ovarian reserve markers with long-term reproductive outcomes are needed, particularly for newer anticancer treatments.

items.title: Menstrual Disorders: Postmenopausal Uterine Bleeding.
items.key: Management of postmenopausal uterine bleeding is based on the underlying cause and can range from hormone therapy to polypectomy for intracavitary polyps or surgical referral for atypical hyperplasia, endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia, or carcinoma. Postmeno-pausal bleeding can also lead to significant patient concern and distress, largely due to fear of underlying malignancy. A systematic, evidence-based approach to postmenopausal uterine bleeding evaluation allows clinicians to diagnose serious pathology early and address patient concerns with clear guidance and follow-up treatment plans.

items.key: Endometrial sampling is indicated in patients at increased risk for endometrial pathology, including those with obesity, chronic anovulation, a family history of malignancy, or age of 45 years or older. Management options include medical and surgical therapies. The levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system is a highly effective medical treatment, whereas hysterectomy remains the most definitive option, particularly for patients who have completed childbearing. Medical management adequately controls symptoms for many, although structural conditions often require procedural or surgical intervention.

items.title: Beyond Layer Count at Caesarean Delivery: A Focused Clinical Review and Trial-Design Framework for Endometrium-Sparing Uterine Closure.
items.key: Current evidence neither identifies a universally superior layer count nor demonstrates prevention of Caesarean scar pregnancy or placenta accreta spectrum by a particular closure strategy. We propose a trial comparing two fully specified, optimized endometrium-sparing packages with equivalent surgeon training and fidelity monitoring, blinded standardized imaging, symptom and reproductive outcomes, and prospective assessment of safety, feasibility, and maternal, operator, and center factors. This framework separates plausible healing mechanisms from demonstrated clinical benefit and defines the comparison needed to determine whether an anatomical third layer adds value.

items.title: Maternal - fetal outcomes and risk factors of uterine rupture in the setting of pregnant women with scarred versus unscarred uterus: a systematic review and meta - analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Compared to patients with scarred uterine rupture, unscarred uterine rupture is associated with significantly higher risks of perinatal mortality, hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage. Additionally, advanced maternal age, a higher incidence of oxytocin, induction of labor, and malpresentation were associated with rupture in the unscarred uterus group. These factors should be taken seriously. Early identification of relevant risk factors is crucial to avoid potential obstetric emergencies, prevent diagnostic delays, and allow timely surgical intervention to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.

items.title: The challenge of Adenomyosis across the ART journey: insights from the Naples Workshop group.
items.key: This expert narrative review integrates available evidence with multidisciplinary clinical expertise to provide practical considerations for patient management while identifying areas of uncertainty and priorities for future research. Overall, management should be individualized according to disease phenotype, symptoms, reproductive potential, previous ART history, and coexisting conditions, while several commonly proposed interventions still require confirmation in well-designed prospective studies.
